issues.title: vectorElemMinSize is quadratic in nesting depth via isVectorVariableLengthType's own…
issues.verdictReason: Benchmarked vectorElemMinSize on a depth-1400 chain of single-dimension nested vectors: ~5.7ms/call (vs. a naively-expected O(depth) cost of microseconds), confirming O(depth^2) behavior. The quadratic blowup comes from isVectorVariableLengthType also recursing through the whole remaining chain at every nesting level, and from unmarshalVector recomputing vectorElemMinSize afresh at each recursive unmarshal level. The exact '5e8 ops' figure in the finding doesn't reconcile with a simple depth^2/2 estimate, but the core claim (re-walks nesting, costly for deep nesting) is verified.
issues.scopeReason: vectorElemMinSize and its use in the new bound check are wholly new code added by this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: vectorElemMinSize recomputes the remaining nesting repeatedly, giving roughly 5e8 operations for a hostile type nested ~1400 deep versus ~1e6 on base; computing variable-length and minimum size in one pass would fix it.

reportedAsByRun.rafp-native-claude-retest-2026-10-09/tid: vectorElemMinSize recomputes the remaining nesting repeatedly, giving roughly 5e8 operations for a hostile type nested ~1400 deep versus ~1e6 on base; computing variable-length and minimum size in one pass would fix it.
